pairs.difference: A sets the orange whistle against pale lemon yellow. B uses stronger golden yellow across the background, bringing hero and backdrop closer in hue and chroma.
pairs.fix: Use a pale lemon-yellow background with softer campfire symbols; keep the whistle orange.

pairs.difference: A has ochre brass and subdued brick-red cord. B pushes the brass toward vivid yellow-orange and the tassels toward intense crimson, with fewer muted colors.
pairs.fix: Draw ochre-gold brass with brown-gold recesses and a muted brick-red cord and tassels.

pairs.difference: A keeps distinct blue rims, green leaves and cool lavender porcelain against red-orange. B's porcelain, flower, leaves and saucer shadows converge toward dusty pink and burgundy, weakening those cool color roles.
pairs.fix: Keep the porcelain white with cool lavender shadows, clear blue rims and flower petals, and fresh green leaves against the red background.

pairs.difference: A uses brighter green cloth and leaves against a stronger purple background. B softens the purple and greens while retaining red apples and orange wicker. Both maintain readable, believable local color roles.

A's wood includes muted brown planks and largely neutral steel bands. B makes nearly all the wood vivid orange and shifts the bands and deck shadow toward purple, producing a more insistently colorful palette.
pairs.fix: Use honey-brown wood with some muted brown planks, neutral gray steel bands, and restrained brown-gray shadows on the deck.

pairs.difference: A balances yellow paint with gray chrome, subdued blue-gray windows and neutral asphalt. B repeats bright cyan through the glass and chrome, with a conspicuous violet road and shadow, adding stronger competing color families.
pairs.fix: Keep the yellow body dominant; use subdued blue-gray windows, neutral silver chrome and gray asphalt with restrained cool shadows.

pairs.difference: A surrounds the yellow tent with muted olive grass and deep blue-green trees. B intensifies the grass and foliage to lime and yellow-green while keeping the tent vivid yellow-orange, leaving little muted color around the hero.
pairs.fix: Surround the golden-yellow tent with muted olive grass and deep forest-green trees; reserve bright yellow-green for a few small leaves.

pairs.difference: A has a subdued gray pot, brown timber and earthy ground, with orange soup and fire as accents. B strengthens orange across the timber, soup and ground while adding vivid greens; the pot also carries stronger blue-purple color.
pairs.fix: Use a neutral charcoal-gray pot, weathered brown timber and muted ochre earth. Keep the strongest orange in the soup and flames, with subdued forest greens.

pattern: Generated cards repeatedly intensify several color regions at once, spread orange through naturally muted materials, or replace neutral rests with cyan and purple. Warm contamination can also collapse distinct cool local colors into pink-brown.
